A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AUTO-CEI and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original appendices A–D match v2 appendices E–H; v2 adds four preceding appendices. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct experiments on BoardgameQA, MATH, and Blocksworld, including benchmark comparisons, curriculum ablations, and reasoning-length and iteration analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original difficulty–length, hyperparameter, and refusal analyses, plus Mistral-7B-Instruct-v3 results on BoardgameQA.

M1.justification: R-Tuning initialization, reward-based trajectory resampling, expert iteration, and curriculum hill climbing remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1–3 and the reward and objective functions. The additional model experiment applies the existing method; the softmax summation-index edit is mathematically equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions use BoardgameQA, MATH, and Blocksworld with the same task coverage. The new analyses reuse these datasets, and the Mistral experiment changes the evaluated model rather than the data or task requirements.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same SFT, vanilla EI, SFT + R-Tuning, EI + R-Tuning, and RLKF (DPO) baselines. New Tables 3–4 reuse existing comparators; the Mistral table uses a subset without removing RLKF from the original experiments.

E3.justification: Supplementary evaluation adds a Mistral-7B-Instruct-v3 configuration on BoardgameQA and accuracy conditional on refusal. Figure 6 compares objective values for lambda = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 across curricula. The original splits, training settings, and main-table protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New appendices A–C test the relationship between difficulty and reasoning length, examine the length distribution, compare lambda-dependent curriculum optima, and measure correctness among refused answers. These substantially expand diagnostics of the central length assumption and refusal behavior. The original curriculum ablations and EI convergence analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly reports Pearson's r = 0.349 and p < 1e-142, while Figure 4 includes standard-error bars for mean reasoning lengths. These are localized additions to statistical reporting; benchmark tables still lack repeated-run uncertainty, and no new seed or run-count information is supplied.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original figures retain their results, but v2 substantially expands the reported evidence. Table 3 adds AUTO-CEI refusal accuracies of 12.25%, 9.89%, and 27.02% across the three tasks. Table 4 adds Mistral results, including 75.01% accuracy, 93.47% precision, and 19.75% refusal rate. Figures 4–6 add difficulty, distribution, and sensitivity findings; these are new results, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces the mathematical definition of refusal accuracy in Equation 3 and describes its complement as a Monte Carlo estimate of awareness of incorrectness. The existing formal model, reward, objective, and optimization assumptions are unchanged. The added complexity discussion supplies conceptual motivation without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and main conclusion retain the same claims about improving reasoning and aligning assertiveness and refusal with model capability. The new appendix evidence supports these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about human-labelled versus model-perceived difficulty and non-standardized reasoning steps. Appendix C acknowledges that true model capacity is hidden and interprets refusal accuracy as an indirect awareness measure. The limitations also frame the simple length metric as a proof of concept and discuss more sophisticated difficulty estimates.

D1.justification: v1 offers code privately upon request; v2 states that code is available and supplies a public repository link. Appendix B adds guidance on reusing previous models when adjusting lambda. Existing data-processing instructions, LoRA settings, sampling parameters, hardware, and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zelikman et al. and Hoffman et al. to the discussion of reasoning self-training, and Wang et al. (2024b) and Damani et al. as possible sources of more sophisticated difficulty estimates. The overall positioning remains unchanged. Kang et al.'s publication update refers to an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. Changes include light copy editing, updated publication and correspondence text, an acknowledgment, expanded limitations, and four new appendix sections preceding the relabelled original appendices. There is no extensive rewrite of the existing exposition.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the empirical displays with three new figures showing difficulty–length relationships, a length histogram, and lambda-dependent curriculum objectives, plus two new tables for refusal accuracy and Mistral results. The original EI convergence figure moves from Figure 4 to Figure 7; the main figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: v2 provides direct checks of the reasoning-length assumption and quantifies correct-answer refusals that v1 only discussed. The additional Mistral experiment and public code link also strengthen evaluation and reproducibility documentation. The gains remain limited: capacity is measured indirectly, the additional model is tested on only BoardgameQA, and benchmark results still lack repeated-run uncertainty.
